title: Probing Ultra-Confined Terahertz Surface Phonon Polaritons in Few-Unit-Cell Freestanding SrTiO3 Membranes by STEM-EELS
content: Surface phonon polaritons (SPhPs) provide unique opportunities for controlling light at subwavelength scales, with potential applications in infrared sensing, imaging, and information processing [1]. However, the narrow Reststrahlen band range of most polar materials limits their applicability across the broad terahertz (THz) and mid-infrared (MIR) bands. Strontium titanate (SrTiO3), a typical perovskite oxide characterized by quantum paraelectricity, superconductivity, and high electron mobility, has recently emerged as a promising SPhP platform due to its giant LO-TO splitting. More intriguingly, with decreasing thickness, the SPhPs in SrTiO3 films are predicted to exhibit extraordinary properties such as high confinement, low group velocity, and good propagation quality, placing SrTiO3 on a par with the two-dimensional van der Waals materials [2, 3].
